target_customer: Sales teams that send follow-up documents and collateral to prospects
problem: Sales follow-up documents sent as email attachments are static and untracked; Quickcard let reps build personalized, interactive sales documents.

founders.name: Rikhav Shah
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Document builder with personalization and view tracking is standard web engineering for a three-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Sales document and proposal tools were abundant and features were easy to copy; no data or network lock-in is documented.

incumbents: Document and proposal tools such as PandaDoc, Qwilr, DocSend
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Quickcard was found; the company went dormant.

market_need_then: The YC description says email attachments were outdated; no spend or demand data was found in sources dated near founding.

branding.domain_note: Held quickcard.com; the domain now shows a parked page that says it may be for sale (observed 2026).

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand assets found; a different Quickcard company from 2015 appears in databases, which suggests the name was confusable.

outcome_analysis: Quickcard was a three-person sales document startup that took a small seed around the Winter 2020 batch and later went dormant, with its domain now parked. No shutdown announcement or reason is public, so no failure factors are assigned; the crowded document and proposal market is context only, not a sourced cause.
notes: The seed round and investors rest on a single third-party site (dead-startups-neon.vercel.app); the amount is not stated there, while CB Insights reports $500K over 3 rounds (unverified, not recorded as a round). The same site names Mathew Pregasen as a co-founder and says the product was earlier called Parsegon and Battlecard, but the YC page lists only Rikhav Shah, so Pregasen is not listed as a founder and the renames are unverified. A PitPro/PitchBook Quickcard founded 2015 in Florida is a different company. Competitor list is empty: the only dated source found (DocSend acquisition by Dropbox, March 2021) is a year after the batch. Cause of dormancy is not public.
